pages.name: GM Guide moved to the wiki

text.content:
Content warning: this module models illicit drugs, addiction, withdrawal and overdose. It is meant for adult tables where that material is welcome. Talk it through before play and use safety tools (Lines and Veils, the X-Card, Script Change).

The full GM Guide for Substances and Paraphernalia lives on the GitHub wiki. The wiki updates between module releases, so it stays current with the latest mechanics, authoring guidance, and troubleshooting notes.

Wiki home

https://github.com/themrbeasley/substances-and-paraphernalia/wiki

What's covered

  • Mechanics overview: the consumption gate, addiction loop, withdrawal and recovery (including the Long Rest Withdrawal Choices dialog), tolerance, and overdose.
  • Dosing others: a drug can be slipped into food or drink, blown into a face, jabbed in or thrown as a gas cloud. The creature it lands on gets the whole dose (the high, the addiction save, tolerance and the overdose check), and the user isn't dosed.
  • Withdrawal length: abstaining at a Long Rest always leads to withdrawal. A passed Constitution saving throw halves its length. When withdrawal ends, the addiction ends.
  • Authoring: the Details-tab fields, the AE name contracts (addict, withdraw, tolerance, overdose), the modifier flag block on bypass effects, the tolerance marker, the overdose flag.
  • Save bypass tiers: automatic success, then reroll on a failure, then advantage, then a bonus (bonuses from several items add up), with worked examples.
  • Poisoned coupling modes: linked-cascade, linked-isolated, independent.
  • Paraphernalia Subtype Manager: adding custom subtypes that authors can pick from.
  • Simulate-dose tool: using the 3-dot menu entry on substance items to dry-run a dose.
  • Macros: Remove Addiction, Remove Altered, Remove Overdose, Remove Tolerance, Remove Withdrawal, Toggle Paraphernalia Enforcement.

Choosing a Save Ability

The Save Ability dropdown defaults to Constitution. By convention, stimulants and performance-enhancers use Constitution (physical dependence); mind-altering substances use Wisdom (psychic compulsion). See the Authoring wiki page for the full convention.

DC scaling intent: shipped substances follow tier-aligned DC ranges (12 to 14 for tier 1, 15 to 17 for tier 2, 18 to 20 for tier 3, 21+ for tier 4 setpiece substances). See the DC Scaling Across Tiers sub-section on the Mechanics wiki for the full pass-rate table and reasoning.

Issues and feedback

Report bugs and request features on the issue tracker.
